dependencies.reason: Supplies outline.Outline, outline.OutlineMany, outline.Options/Source/File/Decl/Backend, the closed kind set, tools.CtagsRunner/ErrCtagsUnavailable and tools.Walk/WalkOptions, which this spec consumes as delivered.

tasks.title: Add file_outline tool with argument handling, disk read and error codes
steps: Write TS-02-1..TS-02-8 in tools/outline_tool_test.go (fake Runner via a SymbolOptions seam, Walk counter, 0000-mode file test skipped as root/Windows) and confirm they fail

Add `SymbolOptions{MaxFiles int; MaxDuration time.Duration; DisableCtags bool; Runner func(ctx context.Context, args []string) ([]byte, error)}` and the field `Symbols SymbolOptions` to tools.Options in tools/tools.go, with only the type and field (no behaviour yet)
Add to fileTools a lazily resolved runner (sync.Once): nil when DisableCtags, Symbols.Runner when non-nil, else CtagsRunner(opts.Env) built on first use; expose it as one method both tools will share

Create tools/outline_tool.go with a `fileOutlineTool` constructor on fileTools: schema path (required string) and include_private (optional bool) via schema.Object/Prop/Opt, Builtin, Parallel, read-only, PromptGuidelines "Before reading a large file, outline it and read only the range you need."

Implement Execute: parse args and reject empty path with invalid_arguments before any filesystem access; check ctx cancelled -> aborted with detail "Operation aborted"; Workspace.Resolve -> path_not_allowed; os.Stat -> read_failed; non-regular -> not_a_file using notAFile; read file bytes; call outline.Outline(ctx, abs, src, outline.Options{Root: workspace root, Runner: runner}); error -> outline_failed with detail
Do not apply the ignore engine or the hidden-entry rule and never touch any symbol table; return a placeholder OK text for now (rendering comes in the next task)
Do NOT register the tool in All() or FileNavigationTools() yet (wiring task does it); tests build the tool from newFileTools directly
Run `go test ./tools -run 'Outline' -count=1` and `make test`

tasks.title: Render file_outline text and data
steps: Write TS-02-9..TS-02-13 using a fake Runner and real Go files and confirm they fail
Implement a pure render function in tools/outline_tool.go producing the header `<rel slash path>  (<backend>, <N> declarations[, <M> unexported not listed])`, the unexported clause only when M>0

List declarations in source order, hiding unexported ones unless include_private is true; each line is two spaces + `L<start>-<end>` padded to align + Signature, or `L<start>` when EndLine is 0 or equals StartLine
Indent a declaration with non-empty Container two further spaces unless its Signature contains the container name

For a file with no declarations render the header and one 'no declarations found' line; when the backend is none add a neutral reason (language not recognised / file too large / binary, derived from the extension, size versus MaxFileBytes and a NUL check) and suggest read_file or search_files
Return Data keys file (the outline.File), backend, declarations (total) and listed (rendered line count); an oversized file must be OK, not an error
Run `go test ./tools -run Outline -count=1`

tasks.title: Build the lazy bounded symbol table and a find_symbol skeleton over it
steps: Write TS-02-32..TS-02-38, TS-02-53 and TS-02-57 (scaled-down MaxFiles variant always runs; 60 000-file variant skipped under -short) and confirm they fail

Create tools/symbols.go with a symbolTable owned by fileTools, created empty (no walk, subprocess or file read at construction): per-file entry {outline.File, size, mtime, indexedAt}, a complete flag, and a Walk seam variable so tests can count/record Walk calls

Implement the build/refresh pass: tools.Walk(ctx, ws, root, WalkOptions{Ignore: fileTools memoized ig, IncludeHidden:false}) from the workspace root, keeping only regular files; skip files whose size and mtime are unchanged; read sources and call outline.OutlineMany in batches of at most 100 with outline.Options{Root, Runner: shared runner}

Enforce SymbolOptions.MaxFiles (default 50 000 when <=0) counting every regular file the walk yields, stopping at the first file past the limit, and MaxDuration (default 2 s when <=0) via context.WithTimeout passed to the walk and OutlineMany; an interrupted batch stays unindexed; distinguish the bound deadline from cancellation of the caller ctx (the latter returns aborted)

When path is given and the table is incomplete, return fs.SkipDir for directories that are neither an ancestor of nor inside path while still walking from the root; a partial table stays incomplete so later passes continue and index only unseen/changed files
Add SymbolPartialMarker(reason string) in tools/limits.go telling the model to narrow with path or fall back to search_files

Create tools/symbol_tool.go: find_symbol constructor on fileTools with schema name (required) and kind, path, exact, max_results (optional), Builtin, Parallel, read-only, PromptGuidelines "Use find_symbol to locate a declaration; search_files for usages and text."; this task's Execute parses args, builds/refreshes the table and returns Data backends, files_indexed, partial, partial_reason, note and a Text header/note (matching and ranking come later); not registered in All() yet
Run `go test ./tools -count=1`

tasks.title: Validate find_symbol input and implement name matching
steps: Write TS-02-14..TS-02-21 over a fixture tree (counting Walk and Runner hooks) and confirm they fail

Validate before any walk: trimmed name non-empty and at most 256 bytes else invalid_arguments; kind trimmed and lower-cased must be in a list of the eleven kinds (func, method, type, class, interface, enum, trait, const, var, module, macro) else invalid_arguments listing them; add a test tying the list to the kinds exported or defined by package outline
Resolve path through Workspace.Resolve (path_not_allowed), os.Stat (read_failed), reject a regular file with invalid_arguments mentioning file_outline; none of this may call Walk
Implement the matcher: default prefix with smart-case (all-lowercase name matches case-insensitively, any uppercase rune makes it case-sensitive); exact=true means exact and case-sensitive
A name containing '.' is compared against Container+"."+Name of declarations with a container; a name without '.' is compared against Decl.Name alone
Apply kind and path filters (path restricts to files under that directory) to produce the candidate matches
Run `go test ./tools -run Symbol -count=1`

tasks.title: Rank, limit and render find_symbol results
steps: Write TS-02-22..TS-02-30 (marker text pinned like the existing marker goldens in tools tests) and confirm they fail

Implement isTestFile per the fixed rule: Go _test.go; Python test_*.py and *_test.py; JS/TS *.test.* and *.spec.*; Java/Kotlin/C#/Ruby base names ending Test, Tests or _spec; any path under a directory named test, tests, __tests__ or spec; and nothing else

Sort matches by exact (smart-case equality counts as exact) before prefix, exported before unexported, non-test before test, shorter path, path, StartLine; use sort.SliceStable with a total key so repeated calls are identical

Add `SymbolResultCap = 50` and `SymbolMarker(limit int) string` to tools/limits.go using capMarker("results", "max_results", limit, SymbolResultCap, ...) with an alternative advising path, kind or exact at the cap
Apply clampLimit(max_results, 20, SymbolResultCap); when matches exceed the limit return the first N, append the marker, set Data truncated and note and ToolMetadata.Truncated with TruncatedByLines

Define SymbolMatch with JSON tags path, backend, kind, name, container, signature, exported, start_line, end_line; Data carries symbols (empty slice, not nil), truncated, note when truncated, backends (name -> indexed files in queried scope), files_indexed (in scope) and partial when applicable

Render Text: header `<N> symbols matching "<name>"  (index: <F> files; <backend> <count>, ...)`, one line `<path>:<start>-<end>  <kind>  <signature>` per match with control characters in the printed path replaced by '?', then marker or partial note; a no-match call is OK with a 'no symbols matched' line and still the index header
Run `go test ./tools -run Symbol -count=1`

tasks.title: Mark the table dirty from write_file, edit_file and the shell tools and refresh dirty paths
steps: Write TS-02-39..TS-02-43 and confirm they fail (a hook records whether the per-path lock is held at mark time)

Add to the symbol table a tiny mutex-protected mark state separate from the abandonable table lock: a set of dirty workspace-relative paths, a whole-table flag and a generation counter advanced by every mark; marking only sets flags and never waits on a build
In write_file and edit_file call table.markDirty(rel) after the write attempt (success or failure) while still holding the per-path lock, before `release()` runs

In All() wrap the Execute of execute, run_command and powershell so the whole table is marked after the command returns for any outcome, passing the result through unchanged; leave executeTool, runCommandTool and PowerShell constructors untouched
In find_symbol, if the table is complete and nothing is marked answer from memory with no Walk or OutlineMany
For each dirty path already in the table: stat it, re-outline it if still a regular file, drop it if gone or not regular; with no whole-workspace walk
A dirty path not in the table or with base name .gitignore escalates to whole-table revalidation (walk-based, reusing the pass from the table task)
Run `go test ./tools -count=1`

tasks.title: Revalidation with racy-mtime window, mark clearing and generation counter
steps: Write TS-02-44..TS-02-46 (blocking fake Runner for the race test; use os.Chtimes to place mtimes) and confirm they fail

Implement revalidation: walk the scope (whole workspace or the part under path with directory pruning) comparing size and mtime of each file; re-outline only files that changed, are new, or whose mtime is within 2 s of their indexedAt; drop entries for files not seen in a completed walk
Drop-unseen applies only for a walk that completed; a pass stopped at a bound never drops entries
Record the generation counter value at the start of each pass; at the end clear only marks (dirty paths and the whole-table flag) that predate that generation
Clear the whole-table mark only when the pass covered the whole workspace and completed within MaxFiles and MaxDuration; leave it set after a path-scoped pass or a bounded pass
Run `go test ./tools -race -run 'Symbol|Table' -count=1`

tasks.title: Abandonable table lock, cancellation semantics and failure containment
steps: Write TS-02-47..TS-02-52 (the race test runs under -race; the source scan test checks that the symbol/outline tool files do not import os/exec and build no sh -c) and confirm they fail

Guard all table state with one context-abandonable lock (a buffered channel of size 1 acquired with select on ctx.Done()); builds, refreshes and reading the table to answer happen under it; a waiter whose ctx ends returns aborted with detail "Operation aborted" without waiting for the build
Ensure the mark path (write_file, edit_file, shell wrappers) uses only the separate flag mutex so it never waits on a build
A cancelled find_symbol ctx during a build or refresh returns aborted (never partial and never marks the table complete); only the MaxFiles/MaxDuration bounds produce partial
Verify that a Runner error or ErrCtagsUnavailable leaves both tools OK with backend naming the fallback (heuristic or go/ast) in file_outline header/Data.backend and find_symbol backends
Confirm all error paths return ToolResults, with no panic or os.Exit
Run `go test ./tools -race -count=1`

Confirm go.mod and internal/policy are unmodified and run `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, `go test ./internal/policy ./tools ./prompt -count=1`, then `make test`
